_schema.description: Hand-verified macroeconomic release values, each traced to the issuing statistical agency's own publication (its API, press release, or bulletin) rather than to a news article, aggregator calendar, or model memory. Built to regression-test the econ_calendar pipeline's handling of revisions, flash-vs-final estimates, exact issuer print formats, confirmed/unchanged re-publications, and seasonally-adjusted vs not-seasonally-adjusted pairs.

fields.country: ISO-3166 alpha-3 or EA20 for the euro area aggregate
fields.issuer: name of the issuing statistical/central agency
fields.series_id: the agency's or FRED's own series code, where one exists
fields.reference_period: the period the figure describes (YYYY-MM or YYYY-Qn)
fields.vintage: first | revised | flash | final -- which edition of the figure this row is, for paired cases
fields.printed_as: the value exactly as the issuer's own release prints it, including its own decimal/sign/percent-sign convention
fields.publication_date: YYYY-MM-DD the issuer released THIS vintage
fields.source_url: the issuer's own page/API call this was read from
fields.case_type: array tagging which golden-set category/categories this row exercises: plain, format, revision, flash_final, unchanged, sa_nsa_pair
fields.related_case: id of the paired vintage/edition, for revision/flash_final/sa_nsa_pair rows
fields.verified: true only when a direct fetch of (or an exact quoted sentence from) the issuer's own release backs the value
fields.confidence: high | moderate-high | moderate -- lower than high means the primary fetch itself could not be completed and the value rests on multiple independent outlets quoting the issuer's release verbatim
fields.notes: verification method, discrepancies vs the unofficial calendar this golden set was built to check, or caveats

excluded_on_purpose: US initial jobless claims (week of ~2026-10-10): BLS/DOL text could not be fetched or corroborated from a primary source; left out rather than guessed.
US industrial production, Sep-2026 (as opposed to the Aug-2026 revision pair below, which WAS verified): the Sep-2026 figure itself could not be confirmed.

US retail sales, Aug-2026 first-vs-revised pair: census.gov could not be reached directly; only secondary outlets quoting the release were found, so the revision pair is left out of this verified set despite being internally consistent across sources.
HCOB/S&P Global Eurozone PMI flash-vs-final (Sep-2026): pmi.spglobal.com could not be reached; secondary-sourced only, left out.

Japan CPI and Canada CPI: corroborated by several independent outlets quoting the respective agency, but the primary stat.go.jp / statcan.gc.ca page itself could not be fetched directly in this pass, so left out of the verified set.

cases.notes: Matches the unofficial calendar figure (3.7%). BLS release text: 'Over the last 12 months, the all items index increased 3.7 percent before seasonal adjustment.'

Same release as the NSA y/y figure above: BLS pairs an NSA y/y headline with an SA m/m headline every month -- the canonical SA/NSA case. Release text: 'increased 0.6 percent on a seasonally adjusted basis in September after rising 0.4 percent in August.'

cases.indicator: CPI-U, All Items Less Food and Energy (core)
cases.notes: Matches the unofficial calendar figure (2.6%).

cases.indicator: CPI-U, All Items Less Food and Energy (core)
cases.notes: BLS release text: 'The index for all items less food and energy rose 0.3 percent in September.'

Matches the unofficial calendar figure (1.3%). BLS: 'The Producer Price Index for final demand increased 1.3 percent in September... the largest advance since rising 1.7 percent in March 2022.' NSA 12-month change +6.3%.
Employment Situation covering August, as first published. Release quote: 'Total nonfarm payroll employment increased by 162,000 in August.'

Employment Situation covering September, which revises August. Exact release sentence: 'the change for August was revised down by 29,000, from +162,000 to +133,000.' No government-shutdown delay was mentioned in either release.
First of BEA's three successive Q2-2026 GDP estimates.

Unchanged-edition case: BEA's own text says 'Real GDP increased at the same rate as in the advance estimate,' even though underlying components (consumer spending, imports) were each revised. Fetched via the FRASER mirror (run by the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis) of BEA's own release text, since the direct BEA PDF for this date returned binary.

Revised up 0.7pp from the second estimate. BEA: 'Real GDP was revised up 0.7 percentage point from the second estimate, primarily reflecting upward revisions to investment, consumer spending, and government spending.' Together with the two entries above this forms a 3-vintage chain (advance=second, second->third revised).

cases.issuer: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
cases.notes: G.17 release text: 'Industrial production (IP) was unchanged in August after increasing 0.2 percent in July.' Capacity utilization 76.3%.

cases.issuer: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
cases.notes: August revised up from 0.0% to 0.1% in the G.17 summary table's 'previous estimate' vs 'revised' columns. The Fed's own text flags a much larger annual benchmark revision (new 2022 base year) planned for 2026-11-24 -- a different, bigger revision event, deliberately not conflated with this routine monthly tweak.
Matches the unofficial calendar figure (3.8%), up from 3.2% in August; above the 3.6% consensus. Eurostat's own convention prints a space before the percent sign.

Confirmed unchanged at 3.8% per Eurostat's regular HICP final-release calendar (17th of the month following the flash). The exact final-release URL/press-release number could not be independently re-fetched in this pass (Eurostat's portal redirected to a login wall on the guessed URL); the 3.8% figure and the 'unchanged' verdict rest on the original research pass plus corroborating secondary coverage, not a fresh direct fetch.
Matches the unofficial calendar figure (-1.1%).
German VPI (national CPI) also +3,3% y/y, +0,6% m/m preliminary. Destatis's own press release uses the comma decimal separator in German ('3,3 %').

Matches the unofficial calendar figure (3.3%). Press release No. 364: 'The Harmonized Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) matched these figures at +3.3% annually' -- confirming the preliminary estimate unchanged. Core (ex food/energy) steady at 2.4%, Destatis President Ruth Brand quoted calling it the year's new inflation high.
Provisional ('estimation provisoire') national IPC, distinct from the harmonized IPCH figures below.

Genuine revision, +0.1pp from the provisional figure: 'consumer prices in France increased by 3.1% over one year in September 2026, revising upward by 0.1 percentage point its preliminary estimate published on September 30.' The exact final-release URL (a specific Informations Rapides PDF number) was not independently pinned down in this pass; the value and date are corroborated by multiple outlets quoting INSEE directly.
France's harmonized index, reported alongside the national IPC in the same INSEE release; up from 2.6% in August.
Confirmed unchanged at 3.4%, unlike the national IPC above which was revised -- a deliberate contrast between France's two CPI measures in the same release.

cases.indicator: NIC (national CPI), All Items incl. tobacco
cases.notes: Fetched directly: 'nel mese di settembre 2026 l'indice nazionale dei prezzi al consumo per l'intera collettivita (NIC), al lordo dei tabacchi, registra una variazione pari a +0,7% su base mensile e a +4,2% su base annua.' m/m +0.7%, up from +3.3% y/y in August.

cases.indicator: NIC (national CPI), All Items incl. tobacco
cases.notes: Fetched directly: final release 'confirming preliminary estimates from 30 September' for the NIC (+4.2% y/y, +0.7% m/m unchanged), while the IPCA harmonized figure below WAS revised in the same release.
m/m provisional +2.0%, up from +3.2% y/y in August.

Genuine +0.1pp revision confirmed directly from Istat: 'The Harmonized Index (IPCA) registers +4.2% year-over-year... The provisional estimate had projected +4.1% annually, so the final figure is 0.1 percentage points higher.' m/m revised to +2.1%.
Fetched directly. INE: 'The annual change in the flash estimate of the CPI stands at 4.9% in September, six tenths higher than the one registered in August.' m/m +0.3%, core 3.1%.

Fetched directly. INE's own text: 'The final figures match the flash estimates released on 29 September 2026... The data published today is final and is not subject to further revision.' Textbook unchanged-edition case, explicitly labelled as non-revisable by the issuer itself.
Reported in the same INE flash release as the national IPC above.
Confirmed unchanged at 5.0% in the same final release as the national IPC.

Matches the unofficial calendar figure (0.1%). ONS: 'Monthly GDP grew by 0.1% in August 2026, following an unrevised growth of 0.4% in July 2026 and a growth of 0.4% in June 2026 (revised up from a 0.3% growth in our previous publication).' That June revision is the paired revision case below.

The 0.3% figure for June is the 'previous publication' value the August-2026 ONS bulletin explicitly revises (see uk_gdp_mm_2026-08's note). It is directly attested as the pre-revision figure in the ONS text fetched for the August bulletin; this entry's own source bulletin (July-2026) and its exact 2026-09-11 publication date were not independently re-fetched in this pass, so confidence is moderate-high rather than high.

Fetched directly from the ONS August-2026 monthly GDP bulletin, which revises June upward from 0.3% to 0.4% while leaving July unrevised at 0.4% -- a clean routine-revision case from the issuer's own text.
